# Start work in the right directory

## Problem statement

When `wl ampa start-work` provisions and enters a *fresh* dev container, the
interactive shell is started with an explicit `cd` to the container-local
sandbox path (`/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`) instead of the canonical
`/workdir/project` symlink. Any already-claimed container is re-entered with
`cd /workdir/project`, so the initial entry is inconsistent with re-entry,
confuses the shell prompt (it computes its relative path against
`/workdir/project`), and makes tooling or user commands that assume
`/workdir/project` report the wrong location.

## Users

- **AI agents** launched into a container by `wl ampa start-work`: they expect
  the project to be at `/workdir/project` so scripts, prompts and `wl ampa
  finish-work` resolve consistently.
- **Operators** reviewing/spawning sandboxes: they expect the documented
  `/workdir/project` path to hold regardless of whether the container was just
  created or re-entered.

### Example user stories

- As an AI agent, when I am dropped into a fresh dev container, I want to be in
  `/workdir/project` so that relative paths, the prompt and tooling match every
  other entry point.
- As an operator, when I run `wl ampa start-work <id>` and then `pwd`, I want to
  see `/workdir/project`, not a `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl ampa start-work <work-item-id>` (and its `sw` alias) starts the
  interactive shell in `/workdir/project` for a newly-provisioned container,
  i.e. `pwd` inside the container reports `/workdir/project` (verification:
  manual E2E `wl ampa sw <id>` then `pwd`).
- [ ] Initial entry is consistent with the already-implemented re-entry and
  legacy-container paths, which both `cd /workdir/project` (verification: code
  inspection + assertion that all interactive entry commands reference
  `/workdir/project`).
- [ ] The shell prompt's relative-path segment resolves against
  `/workdir/project` (no leading `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` shown) and
  `/etc/ampa_bashrc` continues to `cd /workdir/project` (verification: manual
  E2E prompt check).
- [ ] An automated regression test asserts that the interactive entry command
  changes into `/workdir/project` and not the container-local
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` path; the test fails against the
  pre-fix code and passes after the fix (verification: `npm test` /
  `node --test` in the ampa project).
- [ ] Behaviour of `wl ampa finish-work` and the `--wait` / re-entry flows is
  unchanged (verification: existing ampa test suite green).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The container project is physically cloned to
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`; `/workdir/project` is a symlink to it
  created by the setup script. The fix must not move the physical clone.
- Must keep the existing pool/template provisioning, `wl sync` and prompt
  behaviour intact.
- Change is confined to the ampa plugin's `startWork` entry command; the ampa
  project is the implementation repository (see open questions).

## Existing state

- The `start-work` implementation moved out of this repository: the
  `skill/install-ampa/` skill and `ampa.mjs` plugin now live in the **ampa**
  repository (`git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/ampa.git`), under
  `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs`. It was removed from SorraAgents in
  commit `ae0d8474` ("install_ampa skill is now in the ampa proejct itself",
  2026-04-10); the `ampa-repo` git submodule pointer was also removed.
- The container setup clones to `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` and
  creates the symlink `/workdir/project` → that path; `/etc/ampa_bashrc` already
  ends with `cd /workdir/project`.
- Re-entry paths (`start-work` on a claimed pool container / legacy
  `ampa-<id>`) use `cd /workdir/project 2>/dev/null; … exec bash --login`.
- The initial interactive entry in `startWork` used
  `cd ${containerProjectRoot} && exec bash --login` (the `/tmp` path).
- **A fix already exists in the ampa repository on `origin/dev`**: commit
  `77856e0` ("fix: use canonical /workdir/project in start-work initial entry
  (SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW)") changes that one line to
  `cd /workdir/project && exec bash --login`. The matching branch is
  `wl-SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW-fix-start-work-directory`. It is **not yet on
  `main`** (normal dev→main release flow) and the local ampa `dev` checkout is
  one commit behind `origin/dev`.
- The fix commit contains **no automated test** and has not updated the manual
  E2E expectations.

## Desired change

Enter a freshly-provisioned dev container in the canonical
`/workdir/project` directory, matching the re-entry paths, and add regression
coverage so the initial-entry path cannot silently diverge again.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs` (ampa repository) — `startWork()`
  initial interactive entry (`distrobox enter … -c 'cd /workdir/project &&
  exec bash --login'`, currently line ~2137 on the fix branch). Also
  `buildContainerSetupScript()` / `/etc/ampa_bashrc` writer if the canonical
  path is factored out.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-devcontainer.mjs` (ampa repository) — add/extend a
  regression test for the entry command.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-start-work-template-escape.mjs` (ampa repository) —
  nearby start-work setup-script assertions if the path is interpolated.
- `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` (ampa repository) — manual E2E
  expectations / documentation of `/workdir/project`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the fix belongs in the ampa repository, since that is where
  `start-work` lives today; the SorraAgents reference in the commit message is
  the originating work-item ID.
- **Risk:** adding an automated test may require refactoring the entry command
  out of `startWork` into a small exported helper (the command is currently
  built inline and spawned directly), otherwise it is only testable via the
  manual E2E script. Mitigation: extract a pure helper (e.g.
  `buildEntryCommand(cName)`) and unit-test it.
- **Risk:** local ampa `dev` is behind `origin/dev`; implementing from the local
  checkout without pulling would recreate/conflict with the existing fix.
  Mitigation: start from the fix branch / `origin/dev`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** while in the entry code it is tempting to refactor the
  pool/template or prompt logic. Any such extra opportunity should be recorded
  as a separate linked work item, not folded into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MLQ8Z6V20C2FPFP** — "start-work Subcommand" (completed) — defines the
  `wl ampa start-work` behaviour this work item corrects.
- **SA-0MLQ6ZLIO1THWA9O** — "Podman development container for SorraAgents"
  (completed) — parent epic; origin of the `/workdir/project` convention.
- **SA-0MLRGE8T01IHS922** — "When run wl ampa sw do a wl sync" (completed) —
  the `wl sync` behaviour on entry/re-entry, adjacent to this flow.
- **SA-0MLQ8ZT1300Q1MOM** — "list-containers Subcommand" (completed) — related
  container lifecycle command.
- ampa repository commit `77856e0` on `origin/dev` — the existing fix.

## Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The `start-work` code now lives in the ampa repository
  (`SorraTheOrc/ampa`), and the fix for this work item is already committed
  there on `origin/dev` (`77856e0`, referencing SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW), not yet on
  `main`. Should this SorraAgents work item (a) be closed as complete,
  documenting the ampa fix, (b) be migrated/copied to the ampa project's
  worklog (prefix `AM`), or (c) keep additional work in SorraAgents?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the SA implement skill runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree, where the ampa plugin no longer exists, so an
  implementer cannot make the change here without editing another repository.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The ampa fix is a one-line change with no automated
  regression test. Should this work item also add a test asserting the initial
  entry `cd`s to `/workdir/project` (which likely requires extracting the entry
  command into a testable helper), or is manual E2E coverage sufficient?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: no existing test asserts the
  entry command; `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` documents the path but
  is not automated.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** If the fix is accepted as already complete, should the
  SorraAgents work item still record the ampa commit hash/PR and be closed once
  the fix reaches ampa `main`, or closed immediately against `origin/dev`?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the global workflow normally
  closes work items only after the `dev`→`main` release.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MN1M2B810I9YC0U** – Validate Playwright Distrobox compatibility spike (completed)
- **SA-0MPON9P8Z0062VBL** – Child work items created by /plan should start at intake_complete stage (completed)
- **SA-0MKXYO42T0FC6IJR** – Isolated work environments for parallel work (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: container, directory, make, project, right (+3 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)

# Implement the isolation fix

## Goal

Fix the identified root cause so all 5 budget/resume tests pass deterministically in full-repo runs, without masking the flake — satisfying AC2 of SA-0MU7KKJSW006AD5D.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All 5 tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_budget_exceeded_resume.py` pass across at least 5 consecutive full-repo runs.
- No assertion is weakened, no test is skipped or xfailed, and no retry wrapper is introduced to mask the flake.
- Production semantics are unchanged unless the diagnosis in "Diagnose the shared-state leak" proved production code at fault; if so, the justification is recorded in this work item.
- The change is scoped to the audit test suite, or to a shared helper with full-suite verification.
- A comment records the commit hash and the exact commands run.

## Constraints

- Do not serialise the whole suite, add global sleeps, or run tests in a single worker as the fix.
- Keep the blast radius minimal; verify the full project suite if a shared helper changes.

- `skill/audit/tests/conftest.py`

## Goal

Fix `_run_eslint_findings_check` and `_run_eslint_fix_mode` in `linter_runner.py` to filter file targets to JS/TS extensions before invoking eslint, preventing false parsing errors on `.py` and other non-JS/TS files.

## Root Cause

- `_run_eslint_findings_check` (line 351): `cmd = ["eslint", *[str(f) for f in files], "-f", "json", "--quiet"]` passes raw `files` with no extension filter.
- `_run_eslint_fix_mode` (lines 722, 727): same gap in both `fix_cmd` and `rescan_cmd`.
- ESLint v6.4.0 tries to parse `.py` files as JavaScript and emits "Parsing error: Unterminated string constant".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Scoped eslint runs filter file targets to JS/TS extensions; a `.py`-only changed-file list produces zero eslint findings (eslint skipped or given no JS/TS targets).
- [ ] `_run_eslint_findings_check` filters `files` to JS/TS extensions (`.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.ts`, `.tsx`) before building the eslint command.
- [ ] `_run_eslint_findings_check` returns `[]` (skips eslint) when no JS/TS targets remain after filtering.
- [ ] `_run_eslint_fix_mode` filters both `fix_cmd` and `rescan_cmd` to JS/TS extensions only.
- [ ] `_run_eslint_fix_mode` returns `(empty_findings, False)` when no JS/TS targets remain.
- [ ] Non-JS/TS files in the changed-file list are silently skipped (no false-positive findings).
- [ ] Whole-project mode (no explicit files list) is unaffected — it already defaults to JS extensions.

## Key Files

- `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — functions to fix: `_run_eslint_findings_check`, `_run_eslint_fix_mode`
- `skill/code_review/tests/test_linter_runner_eslint_filter.py` — unit tests (see SA-0MUDCVBXM009MFYJ)

## Implementation Notes

- Add a constant `ESLINT_EXTENSIONS = (".js", ".jsx", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".ts", ".tsx")` near the top of the file (or inline in each function).
- In `_run_eslint_findings_check`, before building the command:

  ```python
  if files:
      js_files = [f for f in files if str(f).endswith(ESLINT_EXTENSIONS)]
      if not js_files:
          return []
      cmd = ["eslint", *[str(f) for f in js_files], "-f", "json", "--quiet"]
  else:
      cmd = ["eslint", str(root), "-f", "json", "--quiet"]
  ```

- In `_run_eslint_fix_mode`, apply the same filter in both `fix_cmd` and `rescan_cmd` closures.
- Follow the existing ruff guard pattern at line 392: `py_files = [f for f in files if str(f).endswith(("...",))]`

## Dependencies

- Depends on the unit tests SA-0MUDCVBXM009MFYJ and the regression test SA-0MUDUW8CI008B73L (test-first ordering).
data.title: Fix: filter eslint to JS/TS extensions in scoped-lint path

## Goal

Add a regression/integration test proving that a scoped lint run whose changed-file scope contains only `.py` files completes without an eslint "Parsing error" blocking finding, exercising the real command-construction path (not mocked) with a stub runner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An audit whose changed-file scope contains only `.py` files completes without an eslint "Parsing error" blocking finding (regression).
- [ ] The test invokes `run_eslint` (or the public linter entry point) with a `.py`-only `files` list and a stub `runner` that records the constructed command.
- [ ] Assertion: the recorded command contains no `.py` target (eslint is skipped entirely when no JS/TS files remain).
- [ ] No finding has `severity` of `"high"` or `"critical"` for the `.py`-only scope.
- [ ] Test lives in `skill/code_review/tests/` and passes via the standard test runner.

## Key Files

- `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — public entry point(s) to exercise
- `skill/code_review/tests/test_linter_runner_eslint_filter.py` — shared test module

## Dependencies

- Depends on the unit tests SA-0MUDCVBXM009MFYJ (shared test module).
- This is a test-first item: authored before implementation; it fails until SA-0MUDD7BHE006V3RI lands, which depends on this item.

## Implementation Notes

- Use a stub `runner` callable that returns a controlled result and records the command list, so the test asserts real filtering behaviour without requiring eslint on PATH.
- Assert the `.py` path never appears in any eslint invocation command.

## Problem Statement

Agents repeatedly make the same mistakes when working with pi — using `skill_path` as a bash command instead of the tool, expanding backticks in shell commands, forgetting Python imports, and falling into self-correction loops. A skill that analyses recent session logs to detect these patterns would enable proactive skill improvements and prevent recurring failures.

## Users

- **Agent operator / PI** — receives a structured report of agent confusion patterns and actionable improvement recommendations.
- **Skill authors** — get targeted work items to update SKILL.md files, scripts, or add guardrails.
- **Producers** — understand systemic agent behaviour issues across the project.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Skill reads the last 20 session logs (`.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl`) for the CWD project, sorted by modification time.
2. Heuristic analysis extracts: tool call distribution, thinking-content error signals (keywords: error, fail, retry, incorrect, sorry, wrong, fix, correct, issue, problem, confused, wait, actually, oh, hmm, ah), tool result errors (tracebacks, permission denied, command not found, shell expansion errors), and retry/self-correction patterns.
3. LLM-assisted interpretation (via pi calls) classifies patterns into categories (e.g. "skill invocation confusion", "shell quoting issues", "Python import omissions", "permission issues") and generates recommendations.
4. Structured report rendered in the agent response with: summary of findings, top patterns by frequency, recommended skill improvements, and evidence citations (which sessions showed which patterns).
5. Recommendations are filed as worklog comments on the parent work item.
6. For each actionable recommendation, a child work item is auto-created with issue-type `chore` or `feature`, assigned to Map, and linked via `related-to:<parent-id>` in the description.
7. The skill follows existing project conventions: `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md`, `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/`, `skill/agent-log-review/tests/`.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `docs/dev/agent-log-review-skill-reference.md`).
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Hybrid approach: heuristics for extraction, LLM for classification — not fully automated LLM-only (too expensive) and not heuristic-only (too noisy).
- Only CWD project sessions; no cross-project analysis.
- Auto-create work items but don't implement them — that's downstream work.
- Must handle v3 session log format (session, model_change, thinking_level_change, message types with content as list of thinking/toolCall parts).

## Existing State

- Session logs exist at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl` in v3 format.
- Existing skills follow `SKILL.md` + `scripts/` + `tests/` convention.
- Related work: SA-0MSNYWMJJ002CIJ7 (tag pi sessions spawned from skills with `--session-id`), SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD (24h experiment: measure session length & token use), SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA and reliability recommendations for audit failures), SA-0MLGZN2IH0HH6JSH (Add 'waiting_for_input' session state).
- Known patterns already visible in current sessions: backtick expansion in bash commands, `skill_path` used as bash command, Python `NameError`/`KeyError` from missing imports, `python` vs `python3`, permission denied on script execution, self-correction loops in thinking content.

## Desired Change

A reusable skill that agents can invoke (e.g. `/skill:agent-log-review`) to periodically analyse session logs, produce reports, and auto-create improvement work items.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md` — skill definition and invocation docs
- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — main analysis script
- `skill/agent-log-review/tests/test_agent_log_review.py` — unit tests
- `docs/dev/agent-log-review-skill-reference.md` — skill reference docs

## Risks & Assumptions

**Assumptions**
- Pi v3 session log format is stable (fields: `session`, `model_change`, `thinking_level_change`, `message` with list content of `thinking`/`toolCall` parts, `toolResult` role).
- `<project-slug>` session directory is derived deterministically from CWD (e.g. `--home-rgardler-projects-SorraAgents--`).
- 20 sessions is a statistically useful sample size for common patterns.

**Risks & mitigations**
- **LLM cost/latency** — 20 logs total several MB; mitigate by sending only distilled heuristic signals (counts, excerpts) to the LLM, not raw logs.
- **False positives** — keyword heuristics over-trigger on legitimate uses of "error" (e.g. error-handling code). Mitigate with context windows and LLM confirmation before filing work items.
- **Huge individual sessions** — streaming line-by-line parse, cap per-session excerpt size.
- **Privacy** — session logs may contain paths/tokens; redact secrets in the report and never persist raw log content outside `.worklog/tmp/`.
- **Scope creep** — do not build auto-fix/auto-edit of skills; keep to report + work-item creation (extra opportunities become linked, not in-scope).

## Related work

- SA-0MSNYWMJJ002CIJ7 — Skills: tag pi sessions spawned from skills with --session-id (helps identify skill-spawned sessions for analysis)
- SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD — 24h experiment: AGENTS.md STE100 instruction — measure session length & token use vs previous period (analysis pattern)
- SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL — RCA and reliability recommendations: why audit Phase 1/Phase 2 frequently fail (similar RCA approach)
- SA-0MLGZN2IH0HH6JSH — Add 'waiting_for_input' session state (session analysis infrastructure)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Analysis engine — what approach for pattern detection (heuristic only / LLM-assisted / hybrid)?" — Answer (operator): "hybrid". Source: interactive reply. Research: confirmed existing skills use pi calls (e.g. audit Phase 2) so LLM calls from a skill are an established pattern.
- Q: "Scope — which projects' logs, and where should the report go?" — Answer (operator): "the project from which the skill is initiated (CWD), recommendations filed in the worklog, report returned in agent response". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Recommendations — should the skill auto-create work items, or report-only?" — Answer (operator): "create". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Permission to create the work item?" — Answer (operator): implied by invoking `/intake` with the seed intent; item SA-0MUEKTJRD0010CGC created. Source: interactive invocation.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MS9AXZ8Q007WKKH** – Fix legacy skill/ path refs introduced by StatusLifecycle migration (500d3f8) (completed)
- **SA-0MPDZDVG00013CQJ** – Implement: Agent push-to-dev behavior (completed)
- **SA-0MQBQEPMH000X0NF** – Write tests for auto-fix functionality (completed)

data.description:
Create `pi-client/voice-input/index.ts` — the ExtensionAPI entry point.

**Responsibilities:**
- Register configurable shortcut (default Ctrl+Space) via pi.registerShortcut
- Manage recording state machine (idle → recording → submitting)
- On toggle-start: call doctor.check(), then spawn recorder + whisper-client
- On toggle-stop: finalise transcription, submit via pi.sendUserMessage(), reset state
- Stream partial transcripts into editor via ctx.ui.setEditorText() (replace in-place)
- Show recording status indicator via ctx.ui.setStatus()
- Show error notification via ctx.ui.notify() on any failure (never crash pi)
- On submit: honour pi's busy/steering/follow-up mode

**Key APIs:**
- pi.registerShortcut(Key.ctrl("space"), handler)
- ctx.ui.setEditorText(text) — live partial updates
- ctx.ui.setStatus(text) — recording indicator
- ctx.ui.notify(text, level) — errors
- pi.sendUserMessage(text) — auto-submit

**Unit tests (TDD — write first, mock recorder + worker):**
- Recording state machine transitions (idle→recording→submitting→idle)
- Ctrl+Space toggle starts/stops recording at the right times
- Partial transcript replacement updates editor text in place (no duplication)
- Auto-submit fires a single user message on stop; error paths never throw
Final transcript equals last partial; empty transcript does not submit.
data.title: Extension entry point: shortcut, state machine, editor updates, auto-send
